meta.title: Evolution of NLP — 1962 to 2026
meta.subtitle: From hand-written rules to agentic reasoning

eras.label: Foundations Era
eras.summary: Hand-crafted linguistic rules, pattern matching, and the first chatbots. The field lived or died on whether a small team of linguists could encode enough grammar to fool a human.

milestones.title: ELIZA
milestones.author: Joseph Weizenbaum, MIT
milestones.summary: The first chatbot. Used simple pattern matching and substitution rules (no actual understanding) to simulate a Rogerian psychotherapist. The DOCTOR script became famous; users famously believed it understood them — now called the 'ELIZA effect'.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Demonstrated that even shallow pattern matching could feel human. Founded the entire field of human-computer conversation.

milestones.title: SHRDLU
milestones.author: Terry Winograd, MIT
milestones.summary: An early natural-language understanding program. The user conversed with the computer about a 'blocks world' — moving cubes, naming collections, asking about state. Combined syntax, semantics, and a simulated robot that could actually act.
milestones.why_it_mattered: First system to integrate parsing, semantics, and action in one coherent demo. Showed that grounded language understanding was possible in restricted domains.

milestones.title: Conceptual Dependency Theory
milestones.author: Roger Schank, Stanford → Yale
milestones.summary: A model of language understanding where the meaning of any sentence is reduced to a small set of primitive 'conceptual acts' (PTRANS, ATRANS, etc.). Two sentences with the same meaning get the same representation, regardless of surface wording.
milestones.why_it_mattered: First serious attempt to capture meaning independent of the words used. Inspired a generation of story-understanding systems (MARGIE, SAM, PAM, TaleSpin).

milestones.title: Augmented Transition Networks (ATNs)
milestones.author: William A. Woods, BBN
milestones.summary: An extension of finite-state transition networks with recursive structure and arbitrary conditions on transitions. Became the dominant parsing formalism for NLP through the 1970s and 1980s.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made it tractable to write grammars for real natural-language input. Used in LUNAR (a natural-language interface to a database about moon rocks) and SHRDLU's successor systems.

milestones.title: MARGIE → SAM → PAM → TaleSpin
milestones.author: Schank's group at Yale (Lehnert, Wilensky, Meehan, Cullingford)
milestones.summary: A family of conceptual-dependency-based programs that could infer, paraphrase, summarize, plan, and even tell stories. MARGIE inferred implications; TaleSpin generated short folk tales about bears and bees.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Demonstrated that deep semantic representations could support reasoning and generation — not just parsing. The Yale school defined NLP research for the late 1970s.

eras.label: Statistical Era
eras.summary: Hand-written rules couldn't scale. Researchers turned to probability theory, large corpora, and statistical learning. N-gram language models, HMMs for POS tagging and speech, and the first web-scale MT systems.

milestones.title: Elman Networks (Early RNN for NLP)
milestones.author: Jeffrey Elman, UCSD
milestones.summary: A simple recurrent neural network that learned to predict the next word in a sequence. Each word in the training corpus was encoded as a vector — an early form of word embedding.
milestones.why_it_mattered: First demonstration that neural networks could learn distributed word representations and temporal patterns from raw text. The seed of all later neural NLP work.

milestones.title: LSTM
milestones.author: Sepp Hochreiter & Jürgen Schmidhuber
milestones.summary: Long Short-Term Memory. A recurrent unit with a cell state and three gates (input, output, forget) that mitigates the vanishing-gradient problem and lets RNNs learn dependencies thousands of steps long.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made RNNs actually trainable on long sequences. Dominant sequence model for speech, MT, and text generation from 2010 through 2017.

milestones.title: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy)
milestones.author: Kishore Papineni et al., IBM
milestones.summary: An automatic evaluation metric for machine translation. Compares MT output against professional human reference translations using modified n-gram precision + brevity penalty.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made MT research reproducible at scale. For 20+ years it has been the de-facto standard for evaluating translation systems.

milestones.title: Neural Probabilistic Language Model
milestones.author: Yoshua Bengio et al., Université de Montréal
milestones.summary: Trained a feed-forward neural network to predict the next word given the previous n words. Each word was mapped to a learned distributed representation (a 100-dim vector) before being fed to the network.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Combined two ideas that became the foundation of modern NLP: distributed word representations + neural language modeling. Generalized across vocabulary — same word can have one vector, shared across contexts.

milestones.title: Statistical Machine Translation Goes Mainstream
milestones.author: Google, Moses (Koehn et al.), many others
milestones.summary: Phrase-based statistical MT became the production standard. Google Translate launched in 2006 using this paradigm. Phrase tables + language models trained on parallel corpora replaced rule-based MT.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made working translation systems a real product. Set the stage for the neural MT revolution that came 10 years later.

eras.label: Embeddings & Deep Learning Era
eras.summary: Neural networks returned to NLP — first as word embeddings, then as sequence models. The famous 'king − man + woman ≈ queen' analogy. RNNs and LSTMs dominated, but the seeds of attention and transformers were already planted.

milestones.title: word2vec (CBOW + Skip-gram)
milestones.author: Tomáš Mikolov, Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, Ilya Sutskever, Jeff Dean — Google
milestones.summary: An efficient method to learn word embeddings from huge corpora. Two architectures — Continuous Bag-of-Words and Skip-gram — produced vectors where semantic relationships appeared as linear offsets ('king − man + woman ≈ queen').
milestones.why_it_mattered: Made word embeddings practical at web scale. Showed that simple linear algebra over embeddings captures meaning. Became a default preprocessing step in nearly every NLP pipeline from 2014-2017.

milestones.title: Seq2seq (Sutskever et al.) + Attention (Bahdanau et al.)
milestones.author: Sutskever, Vinyals, Le (Google); Bahdanau, Cho, Bengio (Jacobs University/Montreal)
milestones.summary: Two landmark papers: (1) an encoder-decoder LSTM that maps a variable-length input sequence to a fixed vector and decodes to a variable-length output, achieving state-of-the-art machine translation; (2) attention, which lets the decoder look back at all encoder states with learned weights — solving the bottleneck problem.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Attention directly paved the way for the Transformer (2017). Without attention, there is no GPT, BERT, or any modern LLM.

milestones.title: GloVe (Global Vectors)
milestones.author: Pennington, Socher, Manning — Stanford
milestones.summary: An alternative to word2vec that learns embeddings by factorizing the global word-word co-occurrence matrix of a corpus. Captures the same linear substructure as word2vec but with different training objectives.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Provided a complementary method to word2vec and gave the NLP community a second workhorse embedding technique. Standard pre-trained embeddings (50d, 100d, 200d, 300d) freely available.

milestones.title: TensorFlow released
milestones.author: Google Brain
milestones.summary: Open-sourced deep learning framework built by the Google Brain team. Combined graph-based computation with automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Democratized deep learning research. Made it trivial to share and reproduce architectures — including in NLP — and accelerated the entire field by years.

milestones.title: Google Neural Machine Translation (GNMT)
milestones.author: Wu et al., Google
milestones.summary: End-to-end neural MT system deployed in production at Google. 8-layer encoder + 8-layer decoder LSTM with attention + residual connections. Trained on Google's massive parallel corpora.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Proved that NMT worked at production scale. Within a year Google Translate had switched from phrase-based SMT to GNMT. The 'statistical era' was over.

eras.label: Transformer / LLM Era
eras.summary: The architecture change that changed everything. Self-attention replaced recurrence. Pretrain-then-finetune replaced task-specific architectures. Model size and data scale became the dominant variables. GPT-3 demonstrated emergent in-context learning.

milestones.title: Transformer — 'Attention Is All You Need'
milestones.author: Vaswani et al., Google Brain & Google Research (8 authors)
milestones.summary: Replaced recurrence and convolutions with stacked self-attention + feedforward layers. Parallelizable, faster to train, and stronger on MT than anything before. Introduced multi-head attention, positional encodings, layer norm, and the encoder-decoder pattern that became ubiquitous.
milestones.why_it_mattered: The architecture underlying every modern LLM. The single most important NLP paper of the 2010s.

links.label: Wikipedia: Attention Is All You Need

milestones.title: BERT + GPT-1
milestones.author: Devlin et al. (Google AI Language); Radford et al. (OpenAI)
milestones.summary: Two papers that defined the pretrain-finetune paradigm. BERT is an encoder-only transformer pretrained with masked language modeling + next-sentence prediction. GPT-1 is a decoder-only transformer pretrained with left-to-right language modeling, then fine-tuned on each downstream task.
milestones.why_it_mattered: BERT-style bidirectional pretraining and GPT-style generative pretraining became the two dominant paradigms. Within 18 months every state-of-the-art NLP benchmark was held by a transformer-based model.

milestones.title: GPT-2 + XLNet + RoBERTa + T5
milestones.author: OpenAI (GPT-2); Google Brain (XLNet, T5); Facebook AI (RoBERTa)
milestones.summary: A Cambrian explosion of transformer variants. GPT-2 (1.5B params) showed unsupervised multitask learning at scale. XLNet permuted language modeling. RoBERTa removed BERT's NSP and trained longer with more data. T5 cast every NLP task as text-to-text.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Established that scale + more data + longer training reliably improved quality — the empirical scaling-laws foundation of the LLM era.

milestones.title: GPT-3
milestones.author: Brown et al., OpenAI
milestones.summary: 175-billion-parameter decoder-only transformer. Trained on hundreds of billions of tokens of web text. The 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' paper demonstrated that scale enables in-context learning — the model can perform tasks from just a few examples in its prompt, with no weight updates.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Showed emergent capabilities: arithmetic, code generation, translation, question answering with no fine-tuning. Triggered the commercial LLM race (Microsoft licensed it exclusively the same day it was published).

milestones.title: ChatGPT — RLHF Goes Mainstream
milestones.author: OpenAI
milestones.summary: Released November 30, 2022. GPT-3.5 fine-tuned with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). Became the fastest-growing consumer application in history — 100M users in 2 months.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Brought LLMs to the general public. Sparked the 2023 generative AI boom and the arms race between OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Meta. RLHF became the standard alignment technique.

eras.label: Agentic AI Era
eras.summary: Multimodality, reasoning models, agentic workflows, and open-source catching up. The frontier moved from 'better text generation' to 'tool use, planning, and chain-of-thought'. Reasoning models (o1, o3, DeepSeek-R1) showed that test-time compute scales differently from training-time scale.

milestones.title: GPT-4 + Claude 2 + Llama 2 — The Multimodal Year
milestones.author: OpenAI (GPT-4, March); Anthropic (Claude 2, July); Meta (Llama 2, July)
milestones.summary: GPT-4 added image inputs and dramatically improved reasoning. Anthropic's Claude 2 launched with 100k context. Meta released Llama 2 openly licensed — the catalyst for the open-source LLM ecosystem.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Three competing frontier labs shipping major models within months of each other. Multimodality (vision + text) became standard. Open-weights models became credible alternatives to closed APIs.

milestones.title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet + OpenAI o1 — Reasoning Becomes the Frontier
milestones.author: Anthropic; OpenAI
milestones.summary: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024) jumped to the top of most coding and reasoning benchmarks. OpenAI o1-preview (September 2024) introduced a new paradigm: the model spends additional compute at inference time 'thinking' before responding, producing strong gains on math, science, and code.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Test-time compute scaling emerged as a new axis of progress, separate from parameter scaling. Reasoning chains, search, and self-critique became first-class concerns. MMLU, HumanEval, and other benchmarks were repeatedly saturated.

milestones.title: DeepSeek-R1 + Open-Weight Reasoning
milestones.author: DeepSeek (Hangzhou, China)
milestones.summary: Released January 2025, DeepSeek-R1 matched or exceeded OpenAI o1 on many reasoning benchmarks while being released under an open-weight license. Trained with reinforcement learning from the base model, demonstrating that competitive reasoning models don't require closed infrastructure.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Disrupted the assumption that frontier reasoning was the exclusive domain of well-funded US labs. Triggered a major Nvidia stock sell-off. Accelerated global policy debates on AI export controls.

milestones.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
milestones.author: Anthropic (released November 2024)
milestones.summary: An open standard for connecting LLMs to data sources, tools, and agents. Like USB-C for AI applications — any MCP-compatible model can talk to any MCP-compatible tool.
milestones.why_it_mattered: Standardized the 'tool use' / 'function calling' interface across models. Made agentic workflows portable: write an MCP server once, use it with Claude, GPT, Gemini, or open-source models.

milestones.title: Frontier Reasoning + Agentic Workflows
milestones.author: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta, others
milestones.summary: As of mid-2026, frontier models combine: (a) test-time compute reasoning (chain-of-thought, search, self-critique); (b) tool use via MCP and similar protocols; (c) long context (1M+ tokens); (d) multimodal inputs (text, image, audio, video); (e) agentic loops that plan, act, observe, and iterate autonomously.
milestones.why_it_mattered: The field is moving from 'chat with a model' to 'coordinate an agent that uses tools to accomplish goals'. This is the trajectory set by the 2017 Transformer paper, scaled through 9 years of compute and data growth.
